From 679c04c10d65d32a3f269e696b22912ff0a001b9 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Francesco Lavra <flavra@baylibre.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 11:06:01 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] iio: imu: st_lsm6dsx: Set buffer sampling frequency for
 accelerometer only

The st_lsm6dsx_hwfifo_odr_store() function, which is called when userspace
writes the buffer sampling frequency sysfs attribute, calls
st_lsm6dsx_check_odr(), which accesses the odr_table array at index
`sensor->id`; since this array is only 2 entries long, an access for any
sensor type other than accelerometer or gyroscope is an out-of-bounds
access.

The motivation for being able to set a buffer frequency different from the
sensor sampling frequency is to support use cases that need accurate event
detection (which requires a high sampling frequency) while retrieving
sensor data at low frequency. Since all the supported event types are
generated from acceleration data only, do not create the buffer sampling
frequency attribute for sensor types other than the accelerometer.

Fixes: 6b648a36c200 ("iio: imu: st_lsm6dsx: Decouple sensor ODR from FIFO batch data rate")
Signed-off-by: Francesco Lavra <flavra@baylibre.com>
Cc: <Stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Jonathan Cameron <Jonathan.Cameron@huawei.com>

diff --git a/drivers/iio/imu/st_lsm6dsx/st_lsm6dsx_buffer.c b/drivers/iio/imu/st_lsm6dsx/st_lsm6dsx_buffer.c
index 1ee2fc5f5f1f..5b28a3ffcc3d 100644
--- a/drivers/iio/imu/st_lsm6dsx/st_lsm6dsx_buffer.c
+++ b/drivers/iio/imu/st_lsm6dsx/st_lsm6dsx_buffer.c
@@ -862,12 +862,21 @@ int st_lsm6dsx_fifo_setup(struct st_lsm6dsx_hw *hw)
 	int i, ret;
 
 	for (i = 0; i < ST_LSM6DSX_ID_MAX; i++) {
+		const struct iio_dev_attr **attrs;
+
 		if (!hw->iio_devs[i])
 			continue;
 
+		/*
+		 * For the accelerometer, allow setting FIFO sampling frequency
+		 * values different from the sensor sampling frequency, which
+		 * may be needed to keep FIFO data rate low while sampling
+		 * acceleration data at high rates for accurate event detection.
+		 */
+		attrs = i == ST_LSM6DSX_ID_ACC ? st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs : NULL;
 		ret = devm_iio_kfifo_buffer_setup_ext(hw->dev, hw->iio_devs[i],
 						      &st_lsm6dsx_buffer_ops,
-						      st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs);
+						      attrs);
 		if (ret)
 			return ret;
 	}
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of modifications

### File: `drivers/iio/imu/st_lsm6dsx/st_lsm6dsx_buffer.c`

**What was changed:**  
In the `st_lsm6dsx_fifo_setup()` function, the buffer attributes (`st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs`) are now passed **only** for the accelerometer sensor (`ST_LSM6DSX_ID_ACC`). For all other sensor types (e.g., gyroscope, multiple IDs), a `NULL` pointer is passed instead when setting up the FIFO buffer.

**Why it was changed:**  
Previously, the same buffer attributes (which include the `sampling_frequency` sysfs attribute) were applied to every sensor type. When a user wrote to that attribute for a non-accelerometer/non-gyroscope sensor, the function `st_lsm6dsx_check_odr()` would access the `odr_table` array at index `sensor->id`. That array has only two entries (for accelerometer and gyroscope), so any other index caused an out‑of‑bounds access. Furthermore, the ability to decouple the FIFO sampling frequency from the sensor sampling frequency is only needed for the accelerometer, because all supported event types rely on acceleration data. Restricting the attribute to the accelerometer both fixes the bug and aligns with the actual hardware use case.

### Relationships between modifications

- The change is a single conditional assignment within the loop over sensor IDs.
- It fixes a kernel memory safety issue (out‑of‑bounds read) triggered by any write to the buffer sampling frequency of a non‑accelerometer/gyroscope sensor.
- It also simplifies the driver by not exposing a feature that is hardware‑inappropriate for other sensors.

Here is the root cause:
The buffer sampling frequency attribute was exposed for all sensor types, but `st_lsm6dsx_hwfifo_odr_store()` uses `sensor->id` to index the `odr_table` array, which only has two entries (for accelerometer and gyroscope). Any other sensor ID causes an out-of-bounds access.

Here is the patch:
 
 int st_lsm6dsx_fifo_setup(struct st_lsm6dsx_hw *hw)
 {
 	int i, ret;
 
 	for (i = 0; i < ST_LSM6DSX_ID_MAX; i++) {
+		const struct iio_dev_attr **attrs;
+
 		if (!hw->iio_devs[i])
 			continue;
 
+		/*
+		 * For the accelerometer, allow setting FIFO sampling frequency
+		 * values different from the sensor sampling frequency, which
+		 * may be needed to keep FIFO data rate low while sampling
+		 * acceleration data at high rates for accurate event detection.
+		 */
+		attrs = i == ST_LSM6DSX_ID_ACC ? st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs : NULL;
 		ret = devm_iio_kfifo_buffer_setup_ext(hw->dev, hw->iio_devs[i],
 						      &st_lsm6dsx_buffer_ops,
-						      st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs);
+						      attrs);
 		if (ret)
 			return ret;
 	}
 
 	return 0;
 }

`devm_iio_kfifo_buffer_setup_ext(hw->dev, hw->iio_devs[i], &st_lsm6dsx_buffer_ops, st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs);`
Reason:
This line creates the buffer sampling frequency attribute (`st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs`) for every sensor type (i = 0 to ST_LSM6DSX_ID_MAX). When userspace writes to this attribute for a non-accelerometer, non-gyroscope sensor, the function `st_lsm6dsx_hwfifo_odr_store()` is called, which uses `sensor->id` to index the `odr_table` array (size 2). This causes an out-of-bounds access.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```
attrs = i == ST_LSM6DSX_ID_ACC ? st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs : NULL;
...
devm_iio_kfifo_buffer_setup_ext(hw->dev, hw->iio_devs[i], &st_lsm6dsx_buffer_ops, attrs);
```
Reason:
By conditionally setting `attrs` to `st_lsm6dsx_buffer_attrs` only for the accelerometer (`ST_LSM6DSX_ID_ACC`) and to `NULL` for all other sensor types, the buffer sampling frequency attribute is not exposed for sensors that do not support it. This prevents userspace from triggering the out-of-bounds access in `st_lsm6dsx_hwfifo_odr_store()` while still allowing the accelerometer to have a separate buffer frequency when needed for event detection.
